spec_snapshot.title: Token Bucket Rate Limiter
spec_snapshot.objective: Implement a token-bucket algorithm as the core rate-limiting strategy, supporting configurable burst capacity and steady-state refill rates for fine-grained traffic shaping.

user_stories.i_want: to configure both burst capacity and refill rate per API key
user_stories.so_that: legitimate traffic bursts are allowed while sustained abuse is throttled

user_stories.i_want: the token bucket to integrate with our existing Redis cluster
user_stories.so_that: no additional infrastructure is required for state management

business_rules.description: Each API key is assigned a token bucket with a configurable maximum capacity (default 100 tokens) and a refill rate (default 10 tokens/second).
Tokens are consumed atomically — a request that would cause a negative balance must be rejected rather than partially consuming tokens.
Bucket state must be persisted in Redis with a TTL equal to twice the full-refill duration to prevent stale key accumulation.

acceptance_criteria.title: Token consumption
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is allowed and the remaining count decreases to 9

acceptance_criteria.title: Burst exhaustion
acceptance_criteria.when: A new request arrives before any tokens have been refilled
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is rejected with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header

acceptance_criteria.title: Token refill
acceptance_criteria.given: A bucket with 0 tokens and a refill rate of 10 tokens/second
acceptance_criteria.when: 1 second elapses with no incoming requests
acceptance_criteria.then: The bucket contains exactly 10 tokens (capped at max capacity)

non_functional_requirements.description: Token check-and-decrement operation must complete within 2ms at p99
If Redis is unreachable, the limiter must fall back to a local in-memory bucket with degraded accuracy, logging a warning.
Emit metrics for tokens_consumed, tokens_rejected, and bucket_refills per API key, compatible with Prometheus exposition format.
